title: Retain & Expand: trigger matrix, reconciliation cadence and multi-year incentive scenarios
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem statement: enterprise customers regularly ask for predictable multi-year pricing and clear true-up rules. Current renewal conversations are elongated by ambiguous uplift triggers, inconsistent reconciliation cadence, and lack of standard contractual guardrails for usage spikes or capacity overage. Goal: produce a prescriptive trigger matrix + reconciliation cadence and 3 multi-year incentive scenarios that reduce negotiation cycles, increase expansion conversion rate, and limit downside revenue leakage while preserving customer flexibility. Success criteria: 1) reduce average renewal negotiation time by 30% for deals > $250k ARR, 2) increase expansion conversion velocity (signed upsells within 90d of quota breach) by 20%, 3) limit annualized true-up write-offs to <1% of committed MRR in pilot cohort.
proposed_options: Option A - Quarterly true-up + tiered uplift: quarterly reconciliation with automatic uplift bands: 0-10% over commit (no uplift), 11-40% (standard uplift 1.25x list), >40% (escalator + manual review). Offers standard 3%/yr flat multi-year discount applied to committed spend.

Option B - Annual true-up + graduated multi-year ladder: annual reconciliation with retrospective crediting for overage; multi-year commit ladder (Year1: 0% discount, Year2: 8%, Year3: 12%) where expansion above 25% triggers pro-rata reset to lower discount band. Includes a 60-day grace window for burst traffic with temporary burst credits.

Option C - Hybrid cadence + capped uplift + retention credits: hybrid (monthly metering, annual reconciliation) with capped uplift per quarter (max 20%). Multi-year incentive uses usage-anchored thresholds: deeper discounts for predictable growth trajectories (20%+ CAGR target). Includes contractual clause for capped true-up adjustments and invoice smoothing for enterprise finance teams.

Fallback/legal variant - Contractual safety: add an explicit reconciliation SLA, audit rights for customers, and a one-time reconciliation dispute window of 45 days. Standardize right-to-report metrics and define acceptable measurement sources (Redwood billing + customer usage manifest).
pricing_examples: Example 1 (Option A): Customer commits $300k ARR. Quarterly usage shows Q2 usage +18% => uplift charged at 1.25x list on overage band prorated across quarter; no retrospective credit. Net effect: customer pays $300k + uplift on 18% overage portion.

Example 2 (Option B): Customer commits $600k ARR multi-year: Year1 baseline, Year2 signed at 8% discount if commit sustained; if usage growth >25% in Year2, discount adjusts down to 4% on surplus portion and triggers re-eval for Year3 bands.

Example 3 (Option C): Monthly metering signals burst; capped uplift applies until annual true-up where smoothing credits are applied to normalize for seasonality, protecting long-tail customers from disproportionate quarterly spikes.
metrics: Primary: expansion conversion rate within 90 days of usage breach
Primary: true-up write-offs as % of committed MRR
Secondary: NRR for pilot cohort, churn rate at renewal, legal cycle time for SOW amendments
experiment_design: Cohorts: select 120 enterprise renewals across midmarket and enterprise (>= $200k ARR). Randomize into 3 equal cohorts corresponding to Options A/B/C.
Duration: 6 month pilot with 12 month measurement window for NRR and write-offs.

Analysis: use difference-in-differences for negotiation time and logistic regression for expansion conversion. Minimum detectable effect: 15% relative improvement with alpha=0.05, power=0.8 => ~40 deals per arm.
Guardrails: opt-out path for customers with active compliance constraints; Finance sign-off required on all executed amendments.
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: finalize contract language with Legal & Security; produce standard SOW templates and example clauses for reconciliation cadence and uplift bands.
Week 3-4: Finance runs cashflow and AR modeling; pricing engine updates to support uplift calc and smoothing credits.
Week 5-8: Sales enablement, playbooks, FAQ, and objection handling; pilot rollout to selected cohort of renewals scheduled in Q2.
Post-pilot (Month 7-12): review metrics, gather customer feedback, finalize recommended global policy and product changes (billing UI for smoothing/credits, Console visibility for thresholds).
acceptance_criteria: Legal-approved contract language in Confluence and clause library
Billing system implements uplift calculation and smoothing credit workflow in test environment
Sales playbook and one-pager ready and reviewed by Sales Ops
Finance model shows <1% expected write-off for pilot cohort under chosen option
risk_mitigation: Dispute handling: 45-day reconciliation dispute window + defined escalation path to Revenue Ops
Conservative pilot sizing to limit exposure: cap total committed value in pilot to $25M ARR equivalent
Fallback clause to legacy true-up behavior for customers with unmet security or procurement requirements
Pre-release security review and SSO/KMS checklist for customers requiring nonstandard provisions
